---
title: "ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_application_mapping"
description: "Each application's IBM Verify ID, current name, and first and last event this year."
---

A lookup from IBM Verify application ID to application name, with when each
application was first and last used this year.

Each partition is a full snapshot: one row for every application with an event
between January 1 and that day. Read the latest partition.

`Keywords`: applications, application ID, application name, lookup, first seen, last seen, onboarding

## Provenance

Built from [`application_usage`](../ibm_verify_events_raw/application_usage.qmd)
by `compute_application_mapping()` in the [daily metrics
job](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/ibm_verify_events_streaming/glue_src/ibm_verify_events_metrics_daily.py).

* **Updated**: Daily, at 04:00 ET, for the previous ET day
* **Retention**: While CanadaLogin exists
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Yinlin Zhang](mailto:yinlin.zhang@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://<transformed-bucket>/ibm_verify_metrics/events_application_mapping/`

## Fields

One row per `application_id` per partition.

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| application_id | string | IBM Verify's numeric ID for the application |
| application_name | string | The latest name seen for the application |
| first_seen_at | string | Time of the application's first event since January 1, in UTC (for example, "2026-04-22 12:53:14 UTC") |
| last_seen_at | string | Time of the application's latest event up to the snapshot day, in UTC |
| fetched_at | string | When the job wrote the row, in ISO 8601 UTC |
| date | string | Partition key. The ET day the snapshot covers up to |

## Notes

**`first_seen_at` resets each year.** It is the first event since January 1,
not since launch. For an application's launch date, use `launch_date` in
[`rp.service`](../rp/service.qmd).

**Times are UTC, partitions are ET.** An event late in the ET evening shows the
next UTC day in `last_seen_at`.
